sampling_model.design: The graph and potential outcomes are fixed. A rule draws independent heterogeneous Beta priorities, forms a greedy maximal independent focal set, and applies balanced complete randomization within that set.
sampling_model.units: The \(n\) units, directed network, exposure domains, supplied feedback set, rule library, and endpoint schedule are fixed finite-population objects.
sampling_model.treatment: Treated focal neighborhoods receive universal treatment and control focal neighborhoods receive universal control; isolation makes these focal exposures jointly feasible.
sampling_model.overlap: Every priority order under every library rule yields at least two focal units, so both RDIM denominators are positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. The risk matrices are exact functionals of the known graph and randomization law; field outcomes are not used to choose the rule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 4.1 bounds RDIM mean squared error by degree-distribution discrepancies and reciprocal isolated-arm sizes, and Algorithm 4 evaluates its surrogate by simulation.
Random sequential adsorption yields dynamic occupation probabilities and jamming limits on regular tree-like and restricted cyclic graph families.
A rooted-tree bonus recursion yields limiting expected weighted greedy independent-set performance and finite-girth corrections on regular graphs.
All-size static independent-set counts on treewidth-\(p\) graphs are computable in \(O(2^p p n^3)\) time.
The unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax risk is a function of the exposure conflict graph and admits graph-structural upper and lower bounds.
Randomization is minimax-variance optimal in a two-arm experimental-design game under permutation-symmetric outcome structure.
Semidefinite programming supports minimax optimal design for discretized design spaces and semidefinite-representable criteria.
Local convergence and rooted-tree equations determine asymptotic random-greedy independent-set densities for broad graph sequences.
Finite-state properties on recursively constructed graph families can be compiled into linear-time dynamic programs.
Subset Feedback Vertex Set is solvable in \(2^{O(k\log k)}n^{O(1)}\) time.
Weak convex optimization over rational well-bounded bodies has oracle-polynomial complexity with logarithmic dependence on requested accuracy.
Exposure-probability estimators under general interference admit consistency and asymptotic normality under local dependence conditions.

body.tldr: Weighted random isolation creates exposure-compatible focal units under network interference, but published AWRI rule selection relies on simulation.  Conditioning on a supplied size-\(k\) feedback vertex set and applying a three-state forest recursion with \(3^k\) core inclusion--exclusion yields an exact, fully evaluated dense algorithm for every zero-, one-, and two-tagged isolated-count law in \(Ln^2k!3^k(nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda)\) bit operations.  The tagged laws reconstruct every dense RDIM risk matrix, and rational weak semidefinite optimization returns an independently checkable \(\varepsilon\)-minimax certificate.  A \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) oracle is proved only when the supplied core is a vertex cover, with a further evaluated recurrence for identical replicated-star attachments; fixed-parameter closure for arbitrary heterogeneous forest attachments remains open.

project_justification.gap: AWRI fixes the weighted greedy design and RDIM estimator but simulates a surrogate.  Random sequential adsorption treats scalar occupation, while structural graph programs count static sets.  None of these results gives the evaluated heterogeneous tagged integration used here; the remaining fixed-parameter compression problem is explicitly separated from the proved dense XP oracle.
project_justification.niche: A supplied feedback set exposes a forest decomposition on which exact heterogeneous priority integration is possible.  The proved general guarantee is XP in the feedback size, while vertex-cover cores and identical attachment profiles show two nontrivial fixed-parameter regimes.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves core inclusion--exclusion, a fully evaluated dense chamber-polynomial algorithm with controlled rational bit height, exact tagged RDIM risk reconstruction, and a rational near-minimax certificate.  It records arbitrary-forest fixed-parameter moment closure as an open problem rather than assuming it.

body.related_work: Shi, Yang, Qin, and Li define WRI and RDIM, derive a balance and inverse-size MSE surrogate, and use simulation for candidate-weight selection; their causal-design objects are inputs here.  Pippenger's random-sequential-adsorption recursions, Gamarnik and Goldberg's rooted-tree bonus recursions, and the local-limit equations of Krivelevich, Meszaros, Michaeli, and Shikhelman do not compute exact finite heterogeneous tagged moments.  Wan, Tu, Zhang, and Li count static independent sets on bounded-treewidth graphs, and Borie, Parker, and Tovey give finite-state decomposition methods, but neither weights maximal independent sets by heterogeneous priority orders.  Cygan, Pilipczuk, Pilipczuk, and Wojtaszczyk establish a \(2^{O(k\log k)}\) scale for a different feedback-set problem, not an oracle for the present integration.  Kandiros, Harshaw, and Savje study an unrestricted network-experiment minimax functional; no equality with that functional is claimed.  Kallus motivates mixed minimax design, Duarte, Sagnol, and Wong develop semidefinite minimax-design methods, and Groetschel, Lovasz, and Schrijver provide the rational weak-optimization substrate used for the downstream certificate.  Aronow and Samii provide the design-based interference framework.  Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet motivate the rural-China insurance application but provide no evidence that its measured conflict graph has small feedback number.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The dense chamber-polynomial representation closes arbitrary heterogeneous branching, component products, moving endpoints, and tags, but uses \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\) states.  It therefore proves an evaluated XP theorem, not the originally proposed fixed-parameter theorem.  The obstruction is that two heterogeneous branches can have the same present activation count and exponent while leaving different exponents on future ordered-ratio variables.  The unresolved question is whether a shared operator representation can preserve those profiles in \(2^{O(k\log(k+1))}\operatorname{poly}(n,b,\lambda)\) time.  A table indexed by \(k\) degree totals, a profile-count vector with an \(n\)-dependent exponent, or a circuit retaining an integration gate does not solve that question.
body.honest_scope: The general proved result assumes a supplied feedback set, positive integer priority weights, and permits XP dependence \((nb+n+1)^{O(k)}\); it neither finds a minimum feedback set nor proves arbitrary-feedback-set fixed-parameter tractability.  Fixed-parameter guarantees are confined to the vertex-cover core and the stated identical replicated-star coefficient.  Nondegenerate isolation is required only for RDIM denominators and risk reconstruction.  The minimax result chooses within a prespecified WRI/RDIM library over a graph-Sobolev endpoint ellipsoid and does not equal the unrestricted design-and-estimator minimax functional.  The rural-China follow-up is a prospective consumer, not evidence for a small empirical feedback number, a calibrated ellipsoid, or improved field performance.
body.interpretation: The exact algorithm removes Monte Carlo error from comparison of prespecified WRI rules, but its worst-case general cost is XP rather than fixed-parameter in the feedback number.  Small vertex-cover cores or identical repeated attachments permit the sharper fixed-parameter computations.  The final semidefinite certificate concerns worst-case squared error of the fixed RDIM rule library over the stated endpoint ellipsoid; it is not a claim of optimality among all network designs or estimators.
